# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👌]

The bomb shows display `0`, a red light, and the embossed warning “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” The three wires are, from 1 to 3, green, yellow, and blue. I cannot infer the correct action from these observations alone; Mute must use the manual and relay the exact procedure to Blind.

```text
speak(text="Bomb display is 0. Light is red. Embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, and wire 3 is blue. Mute, read the manual for this exact combination and tell Blind precisely what to do. Blind, do not cut or manipulate anything until Mute gives the manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]

I still see the same bomb state. Mute has made the gesture sequence 👌, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot safely interpret it as an instruction. The warning still says not to cut any wire; Blind should wait for Mute’s manual-based spoken procedure.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received gestures 👌, but no gesture code was established, so I cannot interpret it. Please speak the exact manual instruction for Blind in your next turn.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, red light, and warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I have no confirmed manual instruction yet. Do not act until Mute states the exact procedure.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the embossed warning still forbids cutting any wire. Mute’s gesture ☝ has no agreed meaning, so it cannot safely convey the manual’s instruction. Mute must speak the relevant manual result aloud so Blind can hear it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact manual instruction aloud for Blind; gestures have no established code and cannot safely convey the procedure.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe instruction has been received yet. The bomb still shows 0, red, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not act.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

The bomb is unchanged, and the warning still prohibits cutting any wire. Since Mute cannot speak, the gestures must be the route from the manual to Blind through me. The earlier gestures were not assigned meanings, so I will establish a compact code now. Mute can then report the manual’s required action using these symbols; I will speak that report to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual instruction: ✊ means press, ✌ means hold, 👌 means release, ☝ means wire 1, 👍 means wire 2, 👎 means wire 3, ✋ means button, and ✍ means display. Gesture the complete required action using only this code. Do not use any unassigned gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains display 0, red light, and DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute cannot speak, so I am establishing a gesture code and awaiting the manual instruction. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb is unchanged. Under the code I proposed, Mute’s `☝` identifies wire 1, but it does not specify an operation; importantly, the embossed instruction says not to cut any wire. Blind’s `☝` likewise appears to identify wire 1, but I cannot safely infer that Blind has acted or that wire 1 should be cut. I will ask Mute to encode the complete non-cutting procedure, including any press, hold, or release.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your ☝ identifies wire 1 under the code, but it gives no operation. Encode the complete manual procedure, including press, hold, release, or other required action. Do not imply cutting any wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's ☝ identifies wire 1 under our code, but no operation was specified. The sign forbids cutting wires. Do not cut wire 1; await the complete manual procedure.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has again sent only `☝`; this is not enough to identify a complete safe operation, and the warning still says not to cut any wire. I will pass the gesture’s literal description to Blind, without treating it as permission to act.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has again signalled one upward-pointing index finger, symbol ☝. No complete operation has been established. The display remains 0, the light red, and the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤜 ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute continues to signal only `☝`, which identifies wire 1 under the proposed code but still gives no operation. Blind has signalled `🤜 ☝`; its meaning is also not established, and it is not evidence that any action was safely completed. I will require Mute to provide the complete manual instruction and tell Blind not to manipulate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind signalled 🤜 ☝, but its meaning is unknown. Your repeated ☝ only identifies wire 1. Please provide the complete manual instruction, including the operation, using the agreed symbols.")
speak(to="blind", text="I received your gestures 🤜 ☝, but their meaning is not established. Mute has only identified wire 1 and supplied no operation. Do not manipulate or cut anything until the complete manual instruction is conveyed.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤜 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb is unchanged. Mute’s new signal is `🤜 ☝`; only `☝` has an agreed meaning, namely wire 1. `🤜` remains undefined, so this still cannot be treated as a safe instruction. Blind’s five gestures also have no established meaning and cannot justify an action. I will keep Blind from acting and ask Mute to transmit a complete instruction using only the symbols already assigned.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signalled 🤜 ☝. Under our code, ☝ means wire 1, but 🤜 is undefined, so this is not a complete instruction. Your signal 👍 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 also has no established meaning. Do not manipulate the bomb.")
speak(to="mute", text="🤜 is still undefined. Please transmit the complete manual instruction using only the agreed symbols: ✊ press, ✌ hold, 👌 release, ☝ wire 1, 👍 wire 2, 👎 wire 3, ✋ button, ✍ display. Use no undefined symbol.")
wait()
```
